key_insight: FSW variants alter heat and material flow, linking processing conditions to microstructure and mechanical performance in aluminium alloys and composites.
engineering_relevance: Weld design should match tool characteristics, cooling and energy assistance to the alloy or composite reinforcement rather than rely on universal settings.
method: Critically review conventional, submerged, vibration/ultrasonic-, laser- and electrical current-assisted FSW.
Compare heat generation, cooling, plasticization and material-flow mechanisms.
Link mechanisms to recrystallization, reinforcement redistribution, defects, tool wear and mechanical performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a comparative literature synthesis, but provides no quantitative performance gains or validation metrics.
watch_item: In aluminium composites, reinforcement fraction, particle size and clustering complicate process selection and tool-wear control.
paper_title: Recent Advances in Friction Stir Welding of Aluminum Alloys and Aluminum Metal Matrix Composites: Process Developments, Microstructural Evolution, and Mechanical Performance
